bestBankCandidate.whyNow: Once representations have been unified on a number line, ordering several fractions becomes a clean test of magnitude sense.

bestBankCandidate.exitBridge: Use the ordering to reinforce that every representation refers to one underlying quantity, then move toward comparing two quantities as a ratio.

targetLearnerRealization: A ratio is a repeatable multiplicative batch; scaling one quantity requires scaling the corresponding quantity by the same factor.

bestBankCandidate.whyNow: The sports-car/sedan relationship can literally be displayed as one repeated ratio batch, so the problem's structure is the lesson's core idea rather than incidental context.
bestBankCandidate.entryBridge: After comparing two small groups visually, keep one 4-to-7 batch on screen and ask what happens when the first group grows to the contest target.
bestBankCandidate.reusedRepresentation: Rows of 4 sports-car icons paired with 7 sedan icons.
bestBankCandidate.animationPlan: Start with one batch, let the learner duplicate whole batches until the target first quantity is reached, then count the paired second quantity; only afterward write the proportion notation.
learnerPrompts: How many copies of the original batch do we need?
What must happen to the sedan group when the sports-car group is multiplied by that factor?
bestBankCandidate.exitBridge: Abstract the repeated batch into a:b = ka:kb, then attach units to the two quantities to motivate rates.

generatedTeachingPlan.reason: The authentic bank candidate already isolates multiplicative scaling cleanly and has a visual structure that can be made continuous with the lesson.
generatedTeachingPlan.suggestedShape: Not needed for the core discovery; generated micro-checks may still contrast additive and multiplicative thinking.

bestBankCandidate.exitBridge: Generalize unit tracking as a problem-solving check, then note that rates can be represented by slope later.

targetLearnerRealization: The mean is the level obtained by preserving the total while redistributing it equally.

bestBankCandidate.whyNow: Once learners see average as total/count, a group-average contest problem makes them preserve totals instead of averaging subgroup averages naively.
bestBankCandidate.entryBridge: Keep the equal-share piles on screen, group them into the populations described by the contest problem, and ask what total each group contributes.

bestBankCandidate.exitBridge: Generalize the total = mean × count relationship and distinguish mean from median, mode, and range.

bestBankCandidate.entryBridge: Tell the motion story first and let learners sketch or choose pieces of a graph before revealing the AMC choices.
